proposedAnswers.s1_mechanism: PROPOSAL: git archive, as ruled at toil :140 and the pin header :9, of the pinned commit OID (not the name HEAD) into a fresh mkdtemp directory outside the repo. Extract in-process: a Node tar reader that writes only paths present in the ls-tree inventory and rejects any typeflag other than a regular file, a directory or a pax header, and any unsafe segment. Rationale: no registration in the shared .git/worktrees. A detached worktree per parallel DoD scan would show up in 'git worktree list', which CLAUDE.md's isolation check treats as load-bearing, so it would be a false isolation signal. Also no post-checkout hooks, no .git write, and cleanup is removing a temp directory. Rejected: a detached worktree in snapshot mode (reuse :437-454 with :438 relaxed). That diff is smaller and observeCandidate verifies for free, but it brings registry mutation under concurrency and the isolation-signal hazard. Scanner needs: license-check and gitleaks (--no-git :419) need no .git; gitleaks coverage text :560 must become method-neutral. osv (:236) and semgrep (:172) need no .git, but their target selection without .git is UNMEASURED. The risks are a committed, force-added, gitignored file being dropped, and a tmpdir inside some other git repo (for example a dotfiles home), which would make git discovery select the parent repo and collapse coverage. Requirement: the scanner env sets GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES to the extract's parent. A slice must measure both.
proposedAnswers.s2_identity: PROPOSAL: resolve C = rev-parse --verify HEAD^{commit}, T = C^{tree}, and the inventory = ls-tree -r -z --full-tree C (the :362 shape, by OID, with the same inspectInventory refusals). What replaces observeCandidate on the extract: (a) the extract's file set equals the inventory path set exactly (lstat walk; any symlink, extra or missing file is a mismatch); (b) every file re-hashes to its inventory blob id through ONE 'git hash-object --stdin-paths' process with the work tree set to the extract. It applies git's clean conversion, so the eol=crlf files (.gitattributes:13-14) round-trip; raw in-process hashing would fail on them. UNMEASURED: that archive output round-trips for this repo. (c) The proof runs before the scanners and again after them. (d) The repo's HEAD still resolves to C, and C^{tree} to T, after the scan. inputSha256 = sha256 of the C inventory (the :378 semantics); repositorySha256 as in :371-373.
proposedAnswers.s3_statusAndShape: PROPOSAL: candidate.status = 'snapshot', a new value, never 'clean'. 'clean' is rejected because release-promotion-envelope.mjs:66 and clean-candidate-run.mjs:130 check status, commit and tree WITHOUT the method, so that label would let snapshot evidence through. 'dirty' is rejected because today it means refused or uncertain (:381, pin 2), and a snapshot run on a clean tree would then read 'clean'. The workspace is recorded separately: candidate.workspace = {status: clean|dirty, reason}, from observeCandidate(rootDir) before the scan. So dirty IS recorded, but as the workspace's state, not the candidate's. candidate.snapshot = {method: 'git-archive.v1', verifiedBeforeAfter, contentProof: 'git-hash-object-inventory.v1'}. In snapshot mode verifiedBeforeAfter means (b), (c) and (d) held. It never means the workspace was clean. Top-level evidence.commit must be C, not the late re-read at :1037. candidateUncertain in snapshot mode = !verifiedBeforeAfter, which replaces the shared-tree cleanliness at :1003-1006. That gives pin 1a exit 0, and pin 1b exit 2 through the finding. sourceCapabilityPlan must read the catalog from the extract and run before cleanup (today :780/:631 read rootDir after cleanup :1032).
proposedAnswers.s4_admission: PROPOSAL: snapshot mode writes evidence/security-snapshot-latest.json (plus .v2.json and .v2.verdict.json) and never the security-latest* names (:1059, :1075-1076). Reasons: no gate reads those names; parallel DoD scans then cannot overwrite push-grade evidence; and the v2 envelope is a closed schema validated by the kernel evaluator (gmw :306), so it cannot carry a mode discriminator and can only be separated by path. If the file is copied anyway, the in-band discriminator is defence in depth: guard-push fails at :2251 and :2260, release-promotion at :59 and :66, clean-candidate-run at :147 and :151. Residual risk: a relocated snapshot v2 pair would pass security-completeness-gate :217-222. A push still fails on v1 (:2357 and :2366 run together), but Close (:67) and release-version-plan (:563) consult v2 alone. This is accepted, because the evidence files are agent-writable and only self-hashed, so they are no stronger than today against deliberate forgery. Gates whose contract admits snapshot evidence: NONE (SEC-06 :47, :49). No gate code change is proposed.
proposedAnswers.s5_failureModes: Each is a typed ERROR with classification candidate_snapshot (as :915/:931), giving exit 2 under a blocking gate: snapshot-temp-unavailable (exists, :440); snapshot-archive-failed (non-zero exit or timeout); snapshot-extract-entry-rejected (entry not in the inventory, a non-regular typeflag, or an unsafe path); snapshot-content-mismatch (path-set or blob-id mismatch before the scan, which covers export-ignore and export-subst repos; this repo has none, .gitattributes:2-16); snapshot-mutated-during-scan (the after-proof fails); snapshot-head-moved (HEAD or HEAD^{tree} differs afterwards); plus the existing inventory refusals (:344-347). A cleanup failure sets execution.snapshotCleanup = retained (as :460) and is a non-blocking diagnostic.

proposedAnswers.s7_platformMatrix: Windows: core.autocrlf and .gitattributes eol=crlf both shape the archive output, and the hash-object round-trip covers both (UNMEASURED). Writes from in-process Node avoid MAX_PATH through libuv long paths (UNMEASURED); a worktree would need core.longpaths. Reserved names and trailing-dot or trailing-space path aliases are refused as unsafe paths, extending the :333-348 alias check. WSL: the extract goes in Linux tmp; hash-object is slow if the repo is on /mnt/c (UNMEASURED); the git that archives also hashes, so the config is consistent. macOS: APFS is case-insensitive, which :333-348 covers; tmpdir sits behind the /private symlink, so resolve the realpath before setting the ceiling dirs. Claude: the scan's git calls run inside a node child, outside the Bash guard grammar. Codex: the sandbox may make .git read-only (UNMEASURED); archive only reads .git, which is one argument for it; child EPERM is already typed (:463-469). agy: UNMEASURED; same Node and git contract. Own vs user repos: export-ignore or export-subst gives a typed refusal, never a silent one. For LFS, the archive smudge and the hash-object clean filter writing into .git/lfs are UNMEASURED, and T3 decides whether LFS repos are refused. Submodules and symlinks are already refused (:344-345).
